# Lakana project. Reference: https://lakana-labs.github.io/lakana/how-to/projects/
repo: plant
layers:
  bronze:
    reads: []                                # bronze reads only sources
    write: [append, merge]
    kinds: none
  silver:
    reads: [bronze, silver]
    write: [replace, append, merge, view]
    kinds: [staging]
  gold:
    reads: [silver, gold]
    write: [replace, append, merge, history, view]
    kinds: [fact, dimension, wide]
# Lakana project. Reference: https://lakana-labs.github.io/lakana/how-to/projects/
repo: readings
defaults:
  materialize: table
jobs:
  nightly:
    select: ["silver.*"]
    upstream: true
# Lakana project. Reference: https://lakana-labs.github.io/lakana/how-to/projects/
repo: retail
# The language of the descriptions in the asset headers; translations/de.yaml translates the
# gold tables into German.
main_language: en
defaults:
  materialize: table
requirements:
  fields: [description]
# Layer rules: how data may flow. Bronze reads only sources, silver reads bronze, gold reads
# silver and gold. These are the medallion default; see
# https://lakana-labs.github.io/lakana/how-to/keep-layers-apart/
layers:
  bronze:
    reads: []
    write: [append, merge]
    kinds: none
  silver:
    reads: [bronze, silver]
    write: [replace, append, merge, view]
    kinds: [staging]
  gold:
    reads: [silver, gold]
    write: [replace, append, merge, history, view]
    kinds: [fact, dimension, wide]
# Table health runs at its defaults: every signal warns and none stops a run. To stop a run
# whose row count falls outside the usual band, see the commented line in
# assets/gold/fact_sales.sql and https://lakana-labs.github.io/lakana/reference/table-health/
# Lakana project. Reference: https://lakana-labs.github.io/lakana/how-to/projects/
repo: shop
main_language: en
defaults:
  materialize: table
/* lakana
description: A battery level is between 0 and 100 percent.
on_failure: keep
*/
SELECT sensor_id, battery_pct
FROM bronze.sensor_log
WHERE battery_pct < 0 OR battery_pct > 100
/* lakana
description: A customer's name has no stray spaces around it.
*/
SELECT customer_id, name FROM silver.customers WHERE name <> trim(name)
/* lakana
description: A few hand-written temperature readings.
*/
SELECT 'A1' AS station_id, TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00' AS ts, 1.0 AS temp_c
UNION ALL SELECT 'A1', TIMESTAMP '2026-01-05 00:00:00', 3.0
UNION ALL SELECT 'B2', TIMESTAMP '2026-01-06 00:00:00', 2.0
UNION ALL SELECT 'B2', TIMESTAMP '2026-01-07 00:00:00', 6.0
/* lakana
description: A product's price is above zero.
*/
SELECT product_id, unit_price FROM silver.products WHERE unit_price <= 0
/* lakana
description: A reading that cannot be parsed, so that a run of the job fails.
columns:
  temp_c: The temperature in degrees Celsius.
*/
SELECT CAST('n/a' AS DOUBLE) AS temp_c
/* lakana
description: A sale sells at least one unit.
*/
SELECT sale_id, quantity FROM silver.sales WHERE quantity <= 0
/* lakana
description: A store's name has no stray spaces around it.
*/
SELECT store_id, name FROM silver.stores WHERE name <> trim(name)
/* lakana
description: An average below -90 or above 60 degrees is a sensor fault.
*/
SELECT station_id, avg_temp_c
FROM silver.station_temperatures
WHERE avg_temp_c < -90 OR avg_temp_c > 60
/* lakana
description: An average below -90 or above 60 degrees is a sensor fault.
on_failure: warn
*/
SELECT station_id, avg_temp_c
FROM silver.station_temperatures
WHERE avg_temp_c < -90 OR avg_temp_c > 60
/* lakana
description: An order never has a negative amount.
*/
SELECT order_id, amount_cents
FROM silver.orders_enriched
WHERE amount_cents < 0
/* lakana
description: Each station appears once.
*/
SELECT station_id, COUNT(*) AS copies
FROM silver.station_temperatures
GROUP BY station_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
/* lakana
description: Eighteen generated readings from three weather stations, six days each.
columns:
  station_id: The station that took the reading.
  day: The day of the reading.
  temp_c: The temperature in degrees Celsius.
*/
SELECT
  stations.station_id,
  DATE '2026-01-01' + CAST(days.n AS INTEGER) AS day,
  CAST(stations.base_c + (days.n % 3) - 1 AS DOUBLE) AS temp_c
FROM (VALUES ('A1', 4.0), ('B2', 1.0), ('C3', 9.0)) AS stations(station_id, base_c)
CROSS JOIN (VALUES (0), (1), (2), (3), (4), (5)) AS days(n)
